WSP Parsons Brinckerhoff and DNV GL (2015). Industrial Decarbonisation and Energy Efficiency Roadmaps to 2050 - Iron and Steel (sector report) and Iron and Steel Appendices. Prepared for the Department of Energy and Climate Change (DECC) and the Department for Business, Innovation and Skills (BIS), March 2015. Published at https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/industrial-decarbonisation-and-energy-efficiency-roadmaps-to-2050. No report number or DOI printed.

Region UK (England, Scotland, Wales steel sector), data year 2012-2013 baselines, options to 2050. Two files treated as one source: report (printed 'Page N of 106') and appendices (printed 'Page N of 98'); references give the printed page and table; prefix 'App. C' = appendices, 'main report' = report. LOADED to main file: whole-technology options from the options register (Tables 11-14: top gas recycling retrofit, retrofit with CC, stove flue gas recycling, HIsarna/Corex/Finex rebuild with and without CC, electrolysis, hot charging, near-net-shape casting, endless strip) with TRL, capex per site and CO2 reduction %; process temperatures (Sect. 3.2.3); DC arc furnace electricity use. MEASURES file: all other register options (savings vs practice). NOT LOADED: adoption rates, practical applicability (put in notes), barriers/enablers, pathway model results other than Table 9 summaries, Figure values (chart only). TRAPS: (1) the register gives capex per REPRESENTATIVE APPLICABLE SITE with no site capacity, no cost basis, no price year - all capex rows are flagged PRICE YEAR NOT STATED (2015 used); they are order-of-magnitude estimates the authors say need validation (main report p.82-83). (2) Reductions are CO2 % (C) or electricity % (E), basis (site, process or sector) not stated; 'fuel only' rows have no figure. (3) The 'retrofit with CC' £130M is capture cost only (fn 10) and includes power plant capture (fn 9); the 'advanced with CC' £1,360M combines rebuild and capture. (4) TRL cell '8-98' for stove flue gas recycling is 8-9 with footnote 8 (oxy-combustion capture; post-combustion TRL 7). (5) No payback figures and no process-level specific energy consumption are printed; site-level UK energy intensity 19.6 GJ/t crude steel (final/primary and heating value basis not stated) is in other-values. (6) Options register data sources are mixed literature (US EPA 2012, Berkeley Lab 2010, IIP 2014, NEDO 2008) and expert judgement; numbers are not reprinted from one single work, so no 'reprinted from' tags.
